question:
**Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph.**

A. One morning the Giant was lying awake in bed when he heard some lovely music.

B. Then the Hail stopped dancing over his head, and the North Wind ceased roaring, and a delicious perfume came to him through the open casement. “I believe the Spring has come at last,” said the Giant; and he jumped out of bed and looked out.

C. It was really only a little linnet singing outside his window, but it was so long since he had heard a bird sing in his garden that it seemed to him to be the most beautiful music in the world.

D. It sounded so sweet to his ears that he thought it must be the King’s musicians passing by.
solution:
The correct answer is **'ADCB'**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

**While arranging the parts of the passage, we should find some __grammatical or contextual__ connections between them. Also, the first sentence of a passage is usually independent and introduces a topic. The second one provides more information about it. **

__
 
• Sentence **A **is the independent sentence and talks about how a giant once heard some lovely music. 
 
• So, sentence **A **is the **first **sentence after rearrangement. It sets the scene for the rest of the passage. 
 
• Sentence **D **describes the music the giant heard as being very sweet and explains what the giant thought about the music. Hence, **D follows A.__**
 
• Sentence **C **which describes how the music came from a bird and why the giant thought differently should come after sentence** D**, to maintain continuity on the topic. 
 
• Sentence **B** is the concluding statement of the passage as it provides further information regarding the next occurrences observed by the giant. 
 
• Thus, the correct order after rearrangement is **option 1 i.e. ADCB.**

** So, the correct paragraph is : *****A.** One morning the Giant was lying awake in bed when he heard some lovely music. **D.** It sounded so sweet to his ears that he thought it must be the King’s musicians passing by. **C. **It was really only a little linnet singing outside his window, but it was so long since he had heard a bird sing in his garden that it seemed to him to be the most beautiful music in the world. **B.** Then the Hail stopped dancing over his head, and the North Wind ceased roaring, and a delicious perfume came to him through the open casement. “I believe the Spring has come at last,” said the Giant; and he jumped out of bed and looked out.*
